title: Pump-Insulin Cap on Cartridge Notices: Insulin Pump Program Clinical Pharmacy Questions
content:
**Q. How does the customer's pump insulin limit the expected rate of a cartridge or reservoir liability notice on an Insulin Pump Program?**
The pump-insulin cap follows the customer's Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program — the active insulin pharmacy program whose delivery method is insulin pump — in three cases:

1. Where a written order for its pump insulin dated in the three months before today is on that program, the expected rate is held to no more than the cartridges per 30 days the prescribed dose fills: the newest such order's billing units per 30 days times the insulin each unit holds, divided by the pump's fill per cartridge, rounded up.
2. Where no such order is on it but pump insulin was dispensed under it in the six months before today, it is held to no more than the cartridges per 30 days those dispensings fill: their insulin times 30, divided by the supply days they cover and by the pump's fill per cartridge, rounded up.
3. Otherwise the expected rate is not held.

**Q. What insulin does each unit hold, and what is the pump's fill?**
Pump insulin on that program is its J1817 orders and dispensing at 50 units of insulin per billing unit (the pump insulin unit insulin) on the Insulin Pharmacy Medicare Part B Pump Insulin Program, and its rapid-acting 10 mL vial orders and dispensing at 1000 units per vial (the vial insulin) on any other tier. The pump's fill per cartridge is the Mobi fill of 200 units for a Tandem Mobi, the iLet fill of 160 units for a Beta Bionics iLet and the standard fill of 300 units for every other model.

**Q. When is an order or a dispensing in the three or six months before today?**
An order or dispensing counts as in the three or six months before today when its date is later than the same day of the month three or six months before today.

**Worked cases (hypothetical):**

| Records | Expected rate held to no more than |
|---|---|
| Part B pump insulin program; order dated last month for 66 J1817 units per 30 days; Tandem t:slim X2 | 66 times 50 is 3,300; divided by 300 is 11 |
| Commercial-tier insulin program delivering by pump; order 2 months old for 3 vials per 30 days; Tandem Mobi | 3 times 1000 is 3,000; divided by 200 is 15 |
| No order in 3 months; 4,800 units dispensed over 60 days in the last 6 months; Beta Bionics iLet | 4,800 times 30 is 144,000; divided by 60 is 2,400; divided by 160 is 15 |
| No insulin pharmacy program delivering by insulin pump | not held |
